articles.title: What Does a Telegram Ad Cost? Estimated Prices in 18 Countries (October 2026)
articles.excerpt: A sponsored post in a 100K–500K channel costs about $130 in Russia, $40 in the US, $30 in India and $13 in Egypt. Here is why the spread is so wide. Telegram has no ad marketplace with public rates fo…
articles.body: A sponsored post in a 100K–500K channel costs about $130 in Russia, $40 in the US, $30 in India and $13 in Egypt. Here is why the spread is so wide. Telegram has no ad marketplace with public rates for most of the world. Admins set prices themselves, deals happen in DMs, and the "Telegram ad price" numbers floating around are usually one person's anecdote. We index public Telegram channels for TGMarket , so we estimated the price of one sponsored post for every active channel we can attribute to a country, and summarised it by country. Scope: about 120,000 public channels with 1,000+ subscribers that posted in the last 30 days, in 51 countries. Scam/fake-flagged, adult and shock channels and channels with signs of bought views are excluded.
articles.author: John Rico

articles.title: séance: I let a Gemma ghost haunt my shell (and built it an ofrenda for my deleted files)
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge: Week 4 👻 ezequiel › make test again, you foolish mortal? Exit code two; a familiar echo of my own demise. That line was written by…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge: Week 4 👻 ezequiel › make test again, you foolish mortal? Exit code two; a familiar echo of my own demise. That line was written by a 4-billion-parameter model running on the CPU of a small Linux VM, about three and a half seconds after my test suite failed for the second time in a row. No network request left the machine to produce it. That's the whole project, really: a ghost that lives inside the machine, in the most literal way I could manage. What I Built séance is a haunted terminal. You add one line to your .bashrc (or .zshrc ), and from then on your shell is shared with Ezequiel , a sysadmin who died in 1999 halfway through an fsck and never left the server room.

articles.title: Working in Japan? Here's the "skill sheet" nobody explains to you
articles.excerpt: If you take contract or SES (System Engineering Service) work in Japan, sooner or later an agent will ask for your skill sheet (スキルシート). A skill sheet is an Excel form, not a résumé. A typical one has…
articles.body: If you take contract or SES (System Engineering Service) work in Japan, sooner or later an agent will ask for your skill sheet (スキルシート). What it is A skill sheet is an Excel form, not a résumé. A typical one has: A header: name (often initials only), age, nearest station, certifications One block per project: period, a short description, your role, team size Columns for languages, databases, OS and tools used in that project A row of marks (●) for the phases you handled: requirements, basic design, detail design, coding, integration test, system test, maintenance Clients compare candidates by these sheets, so two numbers matter a lot: years in IT and years per language . ## The annoying parts Every agency has its own layout.

articles.title: Phantom Files: Uncovering the Machine Ghost with Local Open-Weight AI
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 4: Ghost in the Machine "Every file has a story. Some should never have been opened." Phantom Files is an open-source, local-fi…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 4: Ghost in the Machine What I Built "Every file has a story. Some should never have been opened." Phantom Files is an open-source, local-first paranormal forensic workbench that analyzes text files ( .txt , .log , .md ) and crafts fictional, suspenseful case dossiers inspired by their contents. Computing terminology is steeped in occult and supernatural lore: we spawn daemons , terminate zombie processes, diagnose fatal memory corruptions, and debug deadlocks at 03:33:00 UTC. For Week 4's "Ghost in the Machine" theme, Phantom Files takes this metaphor literally.

articles.title: How PyTorch Became the Socket Every AI Chip Plugs Into
articles.excerpt: On 19 October, AWS released TorchNeuron, which lets PyTorch run directly on its Trainium chips. A day later, Google and Meta released TorchTPU, which does the same for Google's TPUs. Both arrived at t…
articles.body: On 19 October, AWS released TorchNeuron, which lets PyTorch run directly on its Trainium chips. A day later, Google and Meta released TorchTPU, which does the same for Google's TPUs. Both arrived at the PyTorch Conference, both are open source, and both connect to PyTorch through the same small hook. That last part is the story. Two companies with no reason to coordinate reached the same conclusion: the road onto a working engineer's laptop runs through one extension point in PyTorch. What happens when you call .to("cuda") Write a + b on two tensors and PyTorch does not immediately add anything. It looks up a name, aten::add , in a table. The part doing that lookup is called the dispatcher.

articles.title: How to Write an Escalation Email Your Leadership Can Act On
articles.excerpt: When a customer escalation needs a decision from your own leadership, send them a short email. Lead with the impact, the status, the owner and the specific decision you need, then the next update time…
articles.body: When a customer escalation needs a decision from your own leadership, send them a short email. Lead with the impact, the status, the owner and the specific decision you need, then the next update time. If the email ends with "please help," leadership still has to work out what you're asking for. Below is one escalation update, field by field, for a made up customer called Larkspur Labs whose EU dashboard is down. It's the internal email to leadership. The customer needs a different email: who owns the problem and when they'll hear next. Subject line: customer, problem, ask Use the form Customer | problem | need: ask . Name the customer, then the problem in a few words, then what you need. Impact Impact is what the problem means for the customer.

articles.title: How 'spacewalking' underwater made me feel like I was really in space
articles.excerpt: Analog Astronaut Commander and Aquanaut Michaela Musilova led underwater simulated “spacewalks” in low visibility to test astronaut safety and communication protocols during simulated space missions.
articles.body: I was breathing just fine through my life support systems, but I kept feeling an urge to double check that everything was ok with my "spacesuit" before heading out on this "spacewalk." I have worn many different types of spacesuits on Earth during my career, but for the first time in my life, I knew that I couldn’t just stop to breathe the air outside if there were an emergency. That's because I was underwater. On this excursion, I was leading a simulated space mission underwater called SEA STAR. My " spacesuit " was actually scuba diving gear, and the simulated spacewalks , or EVAs (Extra-Vehicular Activities), included outings where we explored underwater environments.

articles.title: Astronomers discover the secrets of 'string of pearls' supernova relic and the zombie star at its heart
articles.excerpt: Scientists are still learning about a cosmic 'string of pearls,' a unique celestial relic left by a supernova witnessed by humanity around 850 years ago, which has a zombie star at its heart.
articles.body: Scientists are still learning about a cosmic "string of pearls," a unique celestial relic left by a supernova explosion that humanity witnessed around 850 years ago. That is thanks to the most detailed observation of the dandelion-shaped chains of gas and supernova debris that comprise Pa 30, the only supernova remnant of its type observed in the Milky Way . What makes Pa 30 even more unique is that it has a rare "zombie star" at its heart. Supernovas like the one that created Pa 30 are called Type Ia supernovas; they happen when a dead star called a white dwarf overfeeds on a companion star like a cosmic vampire. This overfeeding triggers a runaway nuclear explosion that usually destroys the white dwarf.

articles.title: Cowboy Space unveils 'Big Iron' rocket to launch 20,000 AI data centers
articles.excerpt: Cowboy Space just gave us our first look at its "Big Iron" rocket, which the company will use to build its AI data center constellation. Big Iron's debut is targeted for late 2028.
articles.body: PALO ALTO, Calif. — Cowboy Space just showed us how it plans to become a big player in the final frontier. The California-based company, which is run by Robinhood co-founder Baiju Bhatt, intends to operate a constellation of 20,000 AI data centers in low Earth orbit (LEO). It will build those satellites in house and launch them on a homegrown rocket — a vehicle Cowboy Space unveiled here on Monday night (Oct. 26), at an event it called "Big Sky Rising." "It's a fundamentally novel approach to rocketry in the modern era, in our opinion," Bhatt said during the event. "The idea is that you have a two-stage rocket where the upper stage of the rocket itself transforms into the satellite." Big Iron's first stage will be reusable.

articles.title: November full moon 2026: When, where and how to see the Beaver Moon
articles.excerpt: Your guide to November's full Beaver Moon, from peak times to skywatching highlights.
articles.body: The November full moon reaches maximum illumination at 9:53 a.m. EST (1453 GMT) on Nov. 24, as the lunar disk sits opposite the sun in Earth's sky, appearing fully lit by its rays. November's full moon is traditionally known as the " Beaver Moon ", because it rises around the time when the small mammals take refuge in their dens, having stored enough food to survive the long winter months, according to the Old Farmer's Almanac . The Nov. 24 full moon also happens to be the first of three consecutive " supermoons ". The non-scientific term is often bestowed on full moons that occur when the natural satellite is within 90% of perigee, when the moon is closest to Earth in its elliptical orbit.
